[Max 2 marks]

There is a positive relationship [1], i.e. as GDP per head increases calorie intake
increases [1]. For example, the USA has a GDP per head of about $60,000 and a
calorie intake of c.3800 kcal, whereas India has a GDP/head of less than $10,000
and a calorie intake of c.2600 kcal [1]. Other anomalies include Kiribati and Niger,
both of which are low-income countries but have a higher-than-expected calorie
intake [1].
[Max 3 marks]

A human factor that affects food supply is over-population/rapid population growth
[1], which can lead to increased demand for food. This reduces the amount of food
available per person [1]. A physical factor is drought [1]. This reduces the amount of
water available to plants and so reduces growth [1].
[Max 4 marks]

Food production can be increased by greater use of fertilisers [1]. This will increase
the amount of nutrients available to crops and enable greater growth [1]. Food
production can also be increased by greater use of irrigation [1]. This is especially
important in dry areas and places with limited water supplies as it enables plants to
grow despite the limited rainfall/water availability [1].
[Max 4 marks]

1970: 225 Tj [1], 2030: 575 Tj [1], an increase of 256% [1] (accept 250–260%).
[Max 3 marks]

Increased the most in absolute size: accept oil and/or gas [1].
Increased the most in relative size: nuclear [1].
[Max 2 marks]

Types of energy sources include renewable and non-renewable sources. Renewable
sources include HEP, solar, tidal/wave, wind, biomass and geothermal. Non-renewable
sources include coal, oil, natural gas, shale oil and nuclear power. Although renewables
are better for the environment they occur in limited locations and can be unreliable,
e.g. wind. In contrast, although non-renewables are polluting and contribute to global
warming, they are widely used where there are large reserves of them and they are
considered to be ‘convenient’. Answer should cover different energy sources and
consider their advantages and disadvantages. There should be an assessment, for
example, of which sources are best but why they might not be the most commonly
used.
[Max 7 marks]
